transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in—what brings you here today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I came in because, well, I've started doing things at work and school that just don't really make sense. I work as a bookkeeping clerk, and lately I've been doing stuff like... lining receipts all the way across the floor. Or I'll sit at my desk and tap the calculator in sets of nine. 

Sometimes I even catch myself just standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I'll just stay like that until someone walks by and asks me if I'm okay. It's just really odd behavior, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to somebody about it.

When you do these things—like lining up the receipts or tapping in sets of nine—do you feel like you're trying to relieve anxiety or an uncomfortable thought that keeps nagging at you, or do they just happen without you feeling any particular urge or worry beforehand?

No, I wouldn't say I'm anxious or anything like that. There's no nagging thought or worry I'm trying to get rid of. It really just... happens. I don't feel any specific urge beforehand, I just kind of find myself doing it. I don't really know why.
Have you noticed anything unusual lately, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs or ideas that others have told you seem unusual or not true?

Actually, yeah, I have noticed something like that. Um... sometimes when I'm alone at my desk at work, or just walking home from class, I'll hear a man's voice. 

He'll say things to me, like... "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It sounds so clear that I always look around to see who's talking to me, but there's never anybody actually there.
Do you have any medical conditions, recent illnesses, head injuries, or use of drugs/medications that started around the same time these behaviors and voice began?

No, not that I know of. I haven't been sick recently, and I definitely haven't hit my head or anything like that. I don't take any medications... well, nothing besides just regular stuff like Tylenol once in a while if I get a headache. And I don't use any drugs. So, yeah, nothing physically has changed.
How long have you been experiencing these unusual behaviors and hearing the voice—has this been going on for days, weeks, or several months now?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say the voices, and... well, that feeling I get that certain numbers are like, messages or something... that's been happening for about eight months.
When you're standing with your hands in the air like that, if someone tries to move your arms or asks you to stop, do you resist or stay rigid, or do you go along easily with what they suggest?

Um, I don't really resist or stay rigid if someone tries to move me. Usually, when I'm standing by the copier with my hands held up like that, I just stay there until someone comes over and asks if I'm okay. Once they say something to me, I usually put them down. 

But honestly, that's kind of why I came in to see you. I've started doing a lot of things at work and school lately that just do not make sense. Like, besides the hands thing, I'll start lining up receipts all across the floor, or I'll catch myself just tapping my calculator in sets of nine. It's just... I don't really know why I'm doing it, but it's definitely not normal for me.
Aside from hearing that voice, have you had any strong beliefs that people are watching you, plotting against you, or trying to control or harm you in some way?

No, I don't think people are plotting against me or trying to harm me. But... well, I do get these really strong beliefs about numbers at work. I know it sounds strange, but I get convinced that certain invoice totals, account numbers, and due dates are actually messages about me. It feels so real. And even when my supervisor sits down and shows me that they are just normal entries, I still have this feeling like... like they are tracking whether I understand the pattern or not. It's hard to shake off.
Have you or people around you noticed that your speech becomes hard to follow, or that your emotional reactions seem flat or don't match what's happening around you?

Well, I don't know about my emotional reactions, but... yeah, my speech has been an issue. Sometimes when I'm trying to explain something at work, like why a ledger is off, I just... my thoughts jump all over the place. I'll start talking about the ledger, and then I'm talking about my tuition deadlines for school, and then tax rules, and then somehow I'm talking about studio lighting and those number patterns I mentioned. People just look at me confused and tell me they have no idea how I got from one point to the next. It makes sense in my head at the time, but I guess it's really hard for anyone else to follow.
Have others told you that your facial expressions or emotional reactions seem unusual—like laughing or smiling when it doesn't fit the situation, or showing little emotion at all?

I haven't really had anyone tell me I laugh at weird times or anything like that. But as far as showing little emotion... yeah, I guess that fits. 

I mean, I still care about people, but most days I just feel really flat. I end up letting texts sit unanswered, and I usually just skip hanging out after class. Even when my friends are talking about things I used to really enjoy, like going to music shows or working on art projects, I just don't have much of a reaction anymore. I just feel flat. So they've probably noticed that I'm not reacting or showing emotion the way I used to.

Aside from the times someone has to prompt you, have you ever noticed yourself staying frozen in one position for a long time on your own, or finding that your body feels stiff or resistant when someone tries to move your limbs, or going through periods where you can't get any words out at all?

I don't really get stiff or completely lose my ability to speak, but... I do get stuck sometimes. Actually, that's a big part of why I came in. I've started doing things at work and school that just don't make sense. 

Like, I'll be at work and just stand by the copier with my hands held up, staying frozen like that until someone comes over and asks if I'm okay. And it's not just that. I'll start lining up receipts all across the floor, or I'll just sit there tapping the calculator in sets of nine. It's really strange, but I just catch myself doing these things.

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of which one happens more often. 

I mean, the freezing up and doing weird things with the receipts definitely happens, but... I don't know if it's happening all the time compared to the other stuff. I guess feeling flat and having my thoughts jump around are pretty much everyday things for me. But the getting stuck part... I just know it happens sometimes. I couldn't really tell you if it's the main issue or just something that happens every now and then.

Have you ever gone through periods where you stopped talking altogether for an extended time, or where your body would resist being moved in a specific direction but then let itself be moved slowly, like bending wax?

No, I haven't ever stopped talking completely like that. I mean, sometimes I'm quiet because I just feel flat, but I can still talk if I need to. And I've never had that thing where my body resists being moved like wax. Like I said before, I do get stuck or frozen sometimes, but it's not like someone is trying to move me and I'm resisting them. I just kind of freeze on my own.

Over the past week or so, would you say the freezing/posturing and repetitive tapping happen almost every day, or are they much less frequent than the disorganized thinking and flat feelings you described?

I'd say the freezing and the tapping are definitely less frequent. They don't happen every day. The flat feelings and the disorganized thinking... those are pretty much constant. I deal with those almost every day. But the getting stuck at the copier or tapping the calculator, that might just happen a couple times a week. It's not an everyday thing.

target_item.manifestation: I still care about people, but most days I let texts sit unanswered, skip hanging out after class, and feel flat even when friends talk about things I used to enjoy, like music shows or art projects.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about flat or unusual emotional expressions, which directly corresponds to the description of Negative Symptoms.

patient.answer:
I haven't really had anyone tell me I laugh at weird times or anything like that. But as far as showing little emotion... yeah, I guess that fits. 

I mean, I still care about people, but most days I just feel really flat. I end up letting texts sit unanswered, and I usually just skip hanging out after class. Even when my friends are talking about things I used to really enjoy, like going to music shows or working on art projects, I just don't have much of a reaction anymore. I just feel flat. So they've probably noticed that I'm not reacting or showing emotion the way I used to.

inference.note: Prominent disorganized speech (derailment) and flat affect support disorganized-type features, while stereotyped motor acts and posturing support catatonic features; absence of prominent persecutory/paranoid delusions makes paranoid type (F20.0) less likely, so it is removed. Because both disorganized and catatonic symptom clusters coexist without one clearly predominating, undifferentiated type (F20.3) is added as a possibility.

doctor.intent: Assess for additional catatonic signs (e.g., waxy flexibility, mutism, or maintaining postures for a long time even without being approached) to determine if catatonic features are prominent enough to meet catatonic subtype criteria versus being incidental to disorganized symptoms
doctor.question: Aside from the times someone has to prompt you, have you ever noticed yourself staying frozen in one position for a long time on your own, or finding that your body feels stiff or resistant when someone tries to move your limbs, or going through periods where you can't get any words out at all?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about additional catatonic symptoms (like staying frozen, stiffness, or mutism). This falls under disorganized or abnormal motor behavior, which corresponds to my symptom S022.

patient.answer:
I don't really get stiff or completely lose my ability to speak, but... I do get stuck sometimes. Actually, that's a big part of why I came in. I've started doing things at work and school that just don't make sense. 

Like, I'll be at work and just stand by the copier with my hands held up, staying frozen like that until someone comes over and asks if I'm okay. And it's not just that. I'll start lining up receipts all across the floor, or I'll just sit there tapping the calculator in sets of nine. It's really strange, but I just catch myself doing these things.

inference.note: Symptoms now include prominent auditory hallucinations with derogatory/command-like content and persecutory-adjacent referential delusions (numbers as messages), reinstating paranoid subtype (F20.0) as a candidate alongside disorganized speech/behavior (F20.1) and catatonic-like posturing without rigidity (F20.2). No single symptom cluster clearly predominates yet, so all three remain viable pending further clarification of catatonic signs (e.g., waxy flexibility, mutism) versus predominance of disorganization or delusional/hallucinatory content.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the relative frequency/dominance of catatonic symptoms versus other symptoms (disorganized speech/behavior and flat affect) to determine if catatonia is the primary feature. The symptom profile does not contain a specific item detailing the relative frequency or dominance of catatonic symptoms compared to others.

patient.answer:
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of which one happens more often. 

I mean, the freezing up and doing weird things with the receipts definitely happens, but... I don't know if it's happening all the time compared to the other stuff. I guess feeling flat and having my thoughts jump around are pretty much everyday things for me. But the getting stuck part... I just know it happens sometimes. I couldn't really tell you if it's the main issue or just something that happens every now and then.

inference.note: Patient reports disorganized speech, flat affect, and occasional catatonic-like posturing/freezing that is not persistent or dominant, alongside hallucinations and referential delusions. Since catatonic features are not the predominant, persistent pattern, F20.2 is now less supported. Paranoid subtype (F20.0) is also less fitting since delusions are referential/bizarre rather than classic persecutory paranoia, and disorganized symptoms are prominent. This leaves a mixed picture best captured by disorganized (F20.1) or undifferentiated (F20.3) subtypes.

doctor.intent: Assess for additional core catatonic signs (e.g., waxy flexibility, mutism, negativism) to determine if catatonia is a prominent, defining feature versus an occasional occurrence within a broader disorganized presentation
doctor.question: Have you ever gone through periods where you stopped talking altogether for an extended time, or where your body would resist being moved in a specific direction but then let itself be moved slowly, like bending wax?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about mutism and waxy flexibility, which are specific catatonic symptoms not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I haven't ever stopped talking completely like that. I mean, sometimes I'm quiet because I just feel flat, but I can still talk if I need to. And I've never had that thing where my body resists being moved like wax. Like I said before, I do get stuck or frozen sometimes, but it's not like someone is trying to move me and I'm resisting them. I just kind of freeze on my own.

inference.note: Disorganized speech, flat affect, hallucinations, and delusions of reference persisting ~8 months support disorganized subtype (F20.1); intermittent catatonic-like posturing/freezing without waxy flexibility or negativism keeps catatonic subtype (F20.3) as a possible but less certain alternative since catatonic features are not clearly dominant or persistent.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the catatonic motor behaviors (freezing/posturing, repetitive movements) occur frequently enough to be the predominant, most prominent clinical feature, compared to how pervasive the disorganized speech and flat affect are in day-to-day life
doctor.question: Over the past week or so, would you say the freezing/posturing and repetitive tapping happen almost every day, or are they much less frequent than the disorganized thinking and flat feelings you described?

target_item.reason: The symptom profile does not specify the exact frequency of the disorganized behaviors over the past week compared to other symptoms.

patient.answer: I'd say the freezing and the tapping are definitely less frequent. They don't happen every day. The flat feelings and the disorganized thinking... those are pretty much constant. I deal with those almost every day. But the getting stuck at the copier or tapping the calculator, that might just happen a couple times a week. It's not an everyday thing.

inference.note: Patient confirms catatonic symptoms (freezing, posturing) are infrequent (a few times/week) while disorganized speech and flat affect are constant/daily, indicating disorganization is the dominant clinical picture rather than catatonia. This rules out F20.3 (catatonic schizophrenia) in favor of F20.1 (disorganized/hebephrenic schizophrenia).

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits 8 months of auditory hallucinations, bizarre delusions (numbers as coded messages), marked disorganized speech (loose associations/derailment), and flat affect that are present nearly daily and are the dominant, persistent features of the illness. Catatonic-like behaviors (posturing, freezing) occur only intermittently (a few times per week) and are not the predominant or persistent clinical picture, ruling out catatonic-type schizophrenia (F20.2). The prominence of disorganized speech and behavior with flat affect, in the absence of a clear systematized persecutory or grandiose delusional system (ruling out paranoid type, F20.0), supports disorganized type schizophrenia. No medical, substance, or mood-episode etiology was identified, and symptoms have persisted well beyond 6 months with functional decline in work and school performance.
